- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ points) — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is neutral or cooling.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings — smooth out extremes by averaging last 5–7 days’ sentiment-weighted price.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by negative, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) — model tends to overfit momentum; use conservative slope adjustment.
